title: Business outcome
question: Do results meet the agreed business threshold, with acceptable trade-offs and viable operating costs?
why: A worthwhile outcome needs measured results and a sustainable full cost, including review and support.
example: Accepted results against the target, a comparable baseline and a costed operating record.
next: Agree the business threshold and acceptable trade-offs; demonstrate that results and full operating costs meet them.

title: Comparable baseline
question: Is the baseline relevant and comparable to this workflow and its intended users?
why: A baseline from a different process may give a misleading comparison.
example: A dated baseline with the same task, population and measurement method, or justified adjustments.
next: Obtain a comparable baseline and document its limitations before relying on the comparison.

title: Current representative testing
question: Do current tests cover the intended scale, users and exceptions on this workflow and model version?
why: Chosen success cases or tests of an old version cannot establish current performance.
example: Sampling and results covering routine work, difficult cases, affected groups and the current version.
next: Test the current version on representative work, users and exceptions at the intended scale.

title: Acceptable quality
question: Do results meet agreed quality and error-severity limits, with no known unacceptable findings?
why: Completing a review is different from accepting its findings. Serious or concentrated failures need resolution.
example: Reviewer acceptance against severity limits, subgroup results and evidence that material failures were resolved.
next: Contain unacceptable output where needed, resolve the findings and obtain an acceptable representative retest.

title: Effective ownership
question: Has a current accountable owner accepted the role with authority, resources and continuity cover?
why: A name alone cannot operate, stop or maintain a workflow.
example: Current role acceptance, stop authority, resources and a workable handover or cover arrangement.
next: Appoint an accountable current owner with authority, resources and continuity cover.

title: Effective human oversight
question: Do necessary approvals and exception handling work under realistic conditions, without routine bypass?
why: An approval step must be practical and effective before it is relied on.
example: A realistic review exercise showing interventions, escalation, workload and prevention of bypass.
next: Demonstrate effective review and exception handling; prevent unreviewed external actions where approval is necessary.

title: Current data permission
question: Are permissions and safeguards current and applicable to the actual data, purpose, tool and proposed use?
why: General tool approval or an old permission does not cover every use. Relevant security and contractual restrictions matter.
example: Current in-scope permission, access/retention safeguards and resolution of relevant security or contractual restrictions.
next: Confirm current in-scope permissions and safeguards with the authorised data/security owner; resolve conflicting or refused approvals.

title: Demonstrated recovery
question: Have proportionate stopping, recovery and containment arrangements been demonstrated for this use?
why: A written plan is insufficient where recovery matters. Some external consequences cannot be reversed.
example: A proportionate stop/recovery exercise and prevention or containment for irreversible effects.
next: Demonstrate stopping and recovery where proportionate; prevent or contain consequences that rollback cannot reverse.

title: Users and sustainable support
question: Can and will intended users operate the workflow, with training, support and sustainable maintenance?
why: Training attendance does not establish a workable accepted process or ongoing support.
example: User acceptance under realistic work, instructions, support, maintenance capacity and continuity arrangements.
next: Resolve user acceptance and workflow fit; provide usable training, support and sustainable maintenance.

title: Monitoring and response
question: Are monitoring, incident response and re-evaluation after material changes workable and owned?
why: A dashboard without a response or current review owner cannot manage a changing workflow.
example: Owned alerts, incident exercises, review dates and triggers for re-testing after material changes.
next: Establish owned monitoring and incident response, review dates and re-evaluation after material changes.
